title: Climate-Control Work: Heat and Refrigerant Precautions
introduction:
Climate-control work brings together different hazards: refrigerant can injure through cold contact or hazardous gas exposure, while heater components can retain enough heat to burn. I match the precaution to the part being serviced before disconnecting anything.

Keep these warnings beside the applicable component procedure and the refrigerant equipment instructions. They establish essential precautions, but they do not replace recovery, charging or component-service instructions. The electric booster heater warning applies when servicing that equipment.

edits.text: WARNING: Liquid air-conditioning refrigerants R-134a and R-1234yf can damage eyes or freeze skin. Always wear safety goggles and avoid contact with liquid refrigerant. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: Refrigerant contact can cause a cold injury. Eye protection and avoiding liquid contact address that hazard.

edits.text: WARNING: Air-conditioning refrigerant gases R-134a and R-1234yf can displace the air needed for breathing in a confined space and can produce toxic gases when burned at high temperatures. Do not release a large quantity of R-134a or R-1234yf gas in a confined space or expose it to a high-temperature flame, such as a torch. Consult the Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) for further information. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury or death.
edits.why: This warning covers separate breathing hazards: loss of breathable air and toxic gases produced by exposure to high-temperature flame. The safety data sheet remains a required information reference.

edits.text: WARNING: Use extreme care when working with refrigerants. Observe all refrigerant safety and service precautions stated on the refrigerant tank and on the recovery and charging equipment. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: The tank and equipment instructions govern their specific handling and operation. This general warning does not replace those instructions.

edits.text: WARNING: Before disconnecting any heater water hoses, shut the engine OFF and wait until it is fully cool. Failure to follow this instruction may result in serious injury or burns from hot liquid escaping from the engine cooling system.
edits.why: Stopping the engine does not immediately remove the cooling system’s retained heat. The fully cool condition must be reached before hose disconnection.

edits.text: WARNING: The electric booster heater can become hot during use and burn unprotected skin. Allow enough time for the heater to cool before servicing it. Failure to follow this instruction may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: When this equipment is being serviced, account for heat retained after use before contacting the heater.
